reasons.evidence:
Thanks for telling me — it’s super frustrating when cards look tiny on paper even if they look normal on the screen.

Why on‑screen = normal but tiny on paper: The default layout is 12" × 12" (true A4). The PDF is sized correctly at 12" × 12". Many browsers/PDF viewers show the page at a visual zoom (often around 50–70%) for convenience, so they look fine on screen. When sent to a real paper size the actual size reveals itself — this is why many printers/print‑shops flag “shrink oversized pages” for a 12" × 12" layout.

Quick checks and fixes:

- Print at 100% / “Actual Size,” not “Fit to page”
  - Choose 100% or Actual Size in the print dialog (not “Fit to page,” which can make everything tiny).
- Paper size must match the export layout
  - The PDF should be sized for A4 (210 × 297 mm). If you chose 10 × 10"/A4 Mixed the OS print settings may need to match the sheet being printed.
- Printer margins/mode
  - Set margins to 10 mm or ¼" and avoid “Resize to fit” or “Auto Fit.” Leave extra margin if your printer driver or print shop needs it to avoid clipping.
- Reduce to a smaller true size (if A4 limits are still an issue)
  - Re‑export from TableCards at 10" × 10" (10×10_A4_Mix). It still prints on A4 but uses a smaller true footprint, giving you a little more breathing room around the edges for borders/prints.
- Verify before printing
  - Preview the card sheet one more time. If everything still looks tiny on the preview or real paper, please tell me:
    - The exact layout you chose (e.g., A4 / 12×12" / 10×10" / Nhật Bàn / Custom size)
    - The paper size and whether you’re printing at home or sending the file to a print shop
    - The exact printer driver or print‑shop workflow you’re using (e.g., “HP OfficeJet, A4, Fit to page engaged”)

With those details I can give closer guidance. In the meantime, usually printing at 100% with A4 margins fixes it.
